method: Fresh independent round-23 full semantic review of every file in inventory.groups.web: all 201 paths (129 implementation/hooks/libraries/styles/configuration/documentation plus 72 tests/fixtures), reading complete file contents, repairing every truncated tool output with bounded follow-up reads. Reviewed authentication and permissions, async initialization, request/draft ownership, ABA navigation, visibility, disconnect and runtime transitions, unknown/accepted receipts, bounded storage/rendering/history, terminal/realtime lifecycle and user-visible recovery. Read current AGENTS.md with the user override of two consecutive clean rounds. Used only current source and this round inventory; no historical audits, WORKLOG, prior repository/Git implementations, old .work reports or report generators. Cross-read assertions in current test files as static evidence without executing a test suite. Independently reproduced the sole finding with the actual current useDraft, Api.beginMutation and operation-store modules, jsdom, fresh fake IndexedDB and deferred synthetic fetch under the fixed Node binary; compared successful persistence against injected browser quota failure and an unmocked application draft-capacity failure. Verified all 1910 raw SHA256 values against inventory.hashes and fixed-Node scripts/snapshot.mjs both before and after review. Source was read-only; only round-specific .work reproduction/evidence/report artifacts were written.

findings.title: Accepted receipt clears newer memory-only draft after persistence failure
findings.description: While submitted draft A awaits its HTTP response, the editable composer accepts newer input B. If persisting B fails, useDraft keeps B in memory and explicitly tells the user the input remains in the page. The accepted A receipt clears the stored revision A and emits a key-only harness-drafts event. The matching hook unconditionally reloads storage, replacing B with an empty draft and clearing the save-failure warning. B was never sent and has no persistent copy, so this is actual user-input loss.
findings.trigger: Persist A; dispatch turn/start through real Api.beginMutation and hold its synthetic HTTP response; type B while persistence fails; release an accepted response for A. Also reproduced with no storage mock using ten 95,000-character drafts and a new 60,000-character B, triggering the application own 1,000,000-character storage bound.
findings.observed: Normal-persistence control retains B. Both injected QuotaExceededError and the unmocked application capacity rejection show B visible before acknowledgement and A still in storage; after acceptance, visible text is empty, the draft storage key is absent, the warning is empty, and the durable operation is accepted. Each scenario dispatches exactly one synthetic request containing A only.

validation.network: Synthetic fetch only; no real HTTP/service calls

findings.minimalFixBoundary: Give draft notifications sufficient mutation/revision identity and apply acceptance cleanup only to the acknowledged in-memory revision. Preserve newer memory-only fields and their persistence warning. A same-key recovery read failure must retain an already mounted current draft, while initial/key-switch loads must still isolate ownership. Do not ignore all notifications: delayed attachment removal from an old unmounted instance must merge its specific removal into the current draft without replacing newer text or retaining the deleted attachment.
focusedRegressionSuggestions: A accepted after B persistence failure: retain exact B revision/content and warning, including the natural aggregate capacity limit.
Repeat with option/context/schema edits and A-to-B-to-A edits; acceptance must not clear a newer revision merely because content matches.
Exercise accepted HTTP, operation reconciliation and explicit acknowledgement paths that share clearDraftSnapshot.
Same-key read failure must not erase valid current memory; first-load corrupt storage and navigation must remain isolated.
Delayed old-instance attachment removal must remove its attachment from a reopened memory-only draft while preserving all other current fields; persistence failure must remain visible.
findings.boundaryAnalysis: Current-instance removeAttachment merges current memory and does not emit a notification if writeDraft throws, so its standalone save failure was not counted as another finding. The readDraft catch clearing current memory and old-unmounted attachment merge are same-root repair/regression boundaries, not separately claimed reproduced findings.

limitations: No full or targeted test suite was run, as required for this frozen audit. Existing tests were read, not treated as passing execution evidence.

The isolated reproduction uses jsdom, fake IndexedDB and synthetic deferred fetch; real browsers, native runtime, microphone, external providers, deployed HTTPS, credentials and network services were not exercised.
One confirmed source-level Web finding; clean status is not claimed and this round cannot count toward consecutive clean rounds.
